## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Field | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Confirmed correctness defect |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium (P2) |
| Task Type | Durable recovery and workflow-label projection |

### What Was Claimed

Issue #147 reports that an interrupted parent merge can leave an issue labeled `workflow:awaiting-merge` even after the merge effect is durably recorded. On restart, recovery projects the merged state and then resumes the persisted `merge-*` node, whose started transition can overwrite that durable projection. The source finding is `CORRECTNESS-001` from PR #145 and references issue #119.

### What We Found

The claim is reproducible by code inspection. `#runParentNode` records the merge effect after the GitHub merge succeeds and before it appends `node.completed`. A crash in that interval leaves a running merge node plus a durable `effectType: "merge"`. During attach, projection reconciliation does not treat that effect as terminal evidence; it can derive `awaitingMerge` from the in-flight node. Even if a merged projection is attempted first, resumed parent recovery unconditionally maps `merge` + `started` to `awaitingMerge` before `findPullRequest`, mergeability resolution, authority checks, or later recovery work. A failure in any of those operations can therefore leave the stale awaiting-merge label.

The existing `directTerminalEvidence` helper validates a merge effect against completed merge evidence for direct terminal cleanup, but it is not used by attach projection recovery and cannot cover the incomplete-node window. Existing rollback and mapping tests do not exercise the attach-to-parent sequence.

### Root Cause

Durable effect precedence is missing at the workflow-label projection boundary. The implementation treats the current parent node transition as newer than the already-recorded merge side effect, although the side effect is the authoritative evidence that the PR merge succeeded. Both attach reconciliation and parent-node restart must recognize a durable merge effect and preserve `workflow:merged` instead of projecting the merge-start `workflow:awaiting-merge` label.

### Affected Files

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Attach reconciliation and resumed parent-node label projection; merge effect recording |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Focused recovery precedence regression coverage |

### Evidence

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`: merge effect is appended immediately after a successful merge and before `node.completed`.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`: `attach()` invokes `#reconcileWorkflowProjection()` and then resumes a persisted parent node such as `merge-1`.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`: `#reconcileWorkflowProjection()` currently derives its stage from the latest node/phase and has no durable merge-effect precedence.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`: `#runParentNode()` unconditionally calls `workflowStageForNodeTransition(node.node, "started")`; `merge` started maps to `awaitingMerge` in `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`.
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts`: current tests at the rollback and lifecycle-mapping sections contain no durable-effect-plus-running-node recovery case.

### History Findings

The source finding identifies PR #145 and issue #119 as the prior context. The current integration snapshot retains merge-effect recording, direct terminal evidence validation, and best-effort awaiting-merge rollback, but no attach/parent-resume regression test. No unrelated historical change is required for this narrowly bounded fix.

### Recommendation

Add a small durable-state predicate and use it in both attach projection reconciliation and parent-node start projection. When the node is `merge` and the run contains a recorded merge effect, project `workflow:merged` and never overwrite it with `workflow:awaiting-merge`, while retaining normal merge-start behavior when no effect exists. Add focused tests for both the interrupted-merge and ordinary-merge cases.

### Related Issues

- Source PR: #145
- Source issue: #119
- Remediation issue: #147

### Decomposition Assessment

This is a single bounded correctness fix. It requires no product, API, UX, policy, security-authority, or cross-worktree decision and should remain limited to `work-on.ts` plus its focused workflow tests.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Validate durable merge-effect precedence for an incomplete/running merge node.
- [ ] Preserve `workflow:merged` during attach and parent-node recovery; do not regress normal merge-start projection.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage for interrupted merge recovery and the no-effect path.
- [ ] Run the required `check` verification and obtain a fresh full correctness/security review of the exact remediation head.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

Attach reconciliation and resumed parent-node projection will both consult the same durable merge-effect predicate before any recovery I/O can overwrite the merged label.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Preserve the authoritative `workflow:merged` issue label whenever a run has a durable merge effect, including the crash window after effect recording and before merge-node completion.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change GitHub merge authorization, mergeability, lease, branch, or protected-branch policy.
- Do not change the state event schema or effect recording semantics.
- Do not change workflow label names or add a domain-specific bypass.
- Do not alter unrelated phases, review roster behavior, issue/PR artifacts, or cleanup policy.
- Do not add credentials, network fixtures, or production issue data to tests.

### Invariants

- A recorded `effectType: "merge"` is durable evidence that `workflow:merged` takes precedence over an in-flight `merge-*` node for label projection.
- A merge node without a durable merge effect continues to project `workflow:awaiting-merge` on its started transition.
- Recovery remains idempotent and may continue the persisted merge node after preserving the merged projection.
- Label projection remains best effort; projection failures do not manufacture a new merge effect or weaken merge authority.
- All changed paths remain inside this contract and the existing required verification command remains authoritative.

### Deliverables

- Add a typed durable-merge-effect predicate and state-aware parent-start stage helper.
- Apply durable merge precedence in attach projection reconciliation and resumed parent-node start projection.
- Add focused tests covering interrupted merge recovery precedence and the normal no-effect path.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| RECOVERY-001 | Durable merge effect selects `merged` for attach/restart projection even while the merge node is incomplete. |
| RECOVERY-002 | `#runParentNode` cannot overwrite a durable merged projection with `awaiting-merge` before recovery I/O. |
| RECOVERY-003 | A merge node with no durable effect retains the existing `awaitingMerge` started-stage behavior. |
| RECOVERY-004 | Focused regression tests and required `check` verification pass. |

### Out of Scope

- Reconstructing a merge SHA from the effect digest.
- Changing merge API retry or read-back behavior.
- Adding a full GitHub integration harness; the pure projection decision is the deterministic seam under test.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- PR #145 introduced the review finding `CORRECTNESS-001`; issue #147 is the bounded remediation.
- The current source already records the merge effect before completing the parent merge node and already has a best-effort label projector.
- Existing direct terminal recovery validates merge effects, but attach projection does not reuse that precedence rule.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `attach()` restores links, reads the durable run, reconciles the issue label, then resumes a persisted parent node.
- `#reconcileWorkflowProjection()` currently derives a stage from run status, latest node, and phase attempts.
- `#runParentNode()` starts/reconciles parent nodes and projects the node's started stage before `findPullRequest`, mergeability, authority, or merge recovery.
- `workflowStageForNodeTransition("merge", "started")` intentionally maps normal in-flight merges to `awaitingMerge`.
- The new helper will distinguish that normal path from a state containing any durable merge effect.

### CI Surface

- Required local verification is the allowlisted `check` command (`npm run check`).
- No new dependency or generated artifact is planned.
- GitHub CI remains parent-owned after PR preparation and exact-head review.

### Prior Findings

- Source finding: `CORRECTNESS-001`, PR #145, reviewed head `62a9b270a121ced818a68d57db622f05a59de290`.
- Current tests cover rollback compensation, direct terminal evidence, and pure lifecycle mappings but not attach-to-parent durable merge precedence.

### Hazards

- Checking only `state.status === "completed"` misses the effect-recorded/node-incomplete crash window.
- Fixing attach reconciliation alone is insufficient because resumed `#runParentNode()` can immediately overwrite the label.
- Applying merged precedence to every node would incorrectly hide later close/cleanup states; scope the override to `node === "merge"` and the durable merge-effect predicate.
- The predicate must not alter the durable state or skip recovery; it only controls label projection.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Architecture Plan

1. Add `hasDurableMergeEffect(state)` as a pure, typed check over the run's recorded effects. (RECOVERY-001)
2. Add `workflowStageForParentNodeStart(node, state)` that returns `merged` only for a merge node with durable merge evidence and otherwise delegates to the canonical started-transition mapping. (RECOVERY-001, RECOVERY-003)
3. Make `#reconcileWorkflowProjection()` project `merged` before deriving in-flight node/phase stages when durable merge evidence exists. (RECOVERY-001)
4. Make `#runParentNode()` use the state-aware start-stage helper so parent recovery cannot overwrite the merged projection, while continuing all existing recovery and completion work. (RECOVERY-002)
5. Add deterministic tests for durable-effect precedence and unchanged no-effect behavior, then run `check`. (RECOVERY-003, RECOVERY-004)

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
